questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A mixture of academically high levels, San Diego's amazing weather, meeting people from all over the world, experiencing something completely new and different

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Cannot recommend doing it more. I thought I was gonna go to Berkeley but I ended up at UCSD and it was the best time of my life. It is the most beautiful place with very good options of traveling a lot around which I took great advantage of

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Very difficult. The advisor did not help me that much. It is honestly a hurdle finding out everything but it is 100% worth it. For UCSD for courses I recommend looking at the courses of the faculty you want to take courses at as well as the the courses they think they are gonna have for the quarter  (they do a tentative schedule of classes:
https://biology.ucsd.edu/education/undergrad/course/course-offerings.html
). In order to find the syllabi (kursusbeskrivelser) for the courses to apply for forhåndgodkendelse use this website:
https://courses.ucsd.edu/
. Do the forhåndgodkendelse early and apply for many more than you'll need, since you are not guaranteed getting the classes you want, although it usually will figure itself out. Even though you study one thing at home i.e. Biochemistry, you can take whatever courses at UCSD if you fulfill the requirements to do so - in other words you are not enrolled as a biochem student but just as an exchange student. For visa application just get it out of the way as early as possible since they will not have tons of spots open for the 'interview' at the embassy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a coordinator but she was not able to answer many questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was barely any help but trust me it'll be fine it's just a lot of work but it's completely worth it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: At UCSD you can live in the International House (I-House), which was the best best experience. They will give you information about the application, it was quite easy. You are not guaranteed a place tho. I think you could be placed in other colleges on campus also but most common if you're not starting in the fall quarter.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Kitchen in the apartment and you have to buy a dining plan with the rent (quite expensive) but that's just the deal. Buy the cheapest plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That is it so fun and social but not overwhelming. Pretty expensive but it's California so everything is super expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not everyone was able to get into I house and

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The system is pretty good. The courses fill up quickly so be ready (you'll get a time slot). BE SURE to do the EASy which is a forhåndsgodkendelse for adding courses at the host university as quickly as possible (you do it through Tritonlink) because it can take some time for the professors to approve the application of enrollment

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have a website where you can see all the courses of the different from the different faculties for me BIO and then they are divided into i.e. BICD, BIPN, BIBC etc., which are subdivisions of the bio department. You can take courses in any of these.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
The Bio faculty can help with some questions:
https://biology.ucsd.edu/about/contact/index.html
.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted. BIMM 134 Biology of Cancer with Michael Burg was super nice. BIMM 140 Immunology is hard. If you like neuro BIPN 140 Cellular Neurobiology is good. I took a graduate course (kandidat/phd level) BIOM 156 Fundamentals of Cancer Biology, really good but also challenging.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do the EASy request early on

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wish there had been better course offerings in the fall quarter but winter was perfect.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: More work than at UCPH (homework, assignments, midterms etc.) but in general it is more memorization and less applied.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The quarter system is intense but not so intense could cant go on trips and have a lot of fun.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BICD140 Immunology
BIPN140 Cellular neurobiology
BIMM 112 Regulation of Eukaryotic Gene Expression
BIMM 134 Biology of Cancer
HILD 30 History of Public Health
MUS 95D Symphonic Chorus
BIOM 256 Fundementals of Cancer Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Already stated earlier

questions.answer: Health insurance is $898 per quarter (get it through the university, you will need it)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and basically everything is so expensive but that is just what you have to settle with

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of clubs but I didn't engage that much but could've been fun. I had a choir: Symphonic chorus which was fun. There aren't a lot of official sports: basketball is nice. The gym is free and super nice, there are swimming pools and many recreational facilities (sports facilities).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Tons of clubs and mostly activities going on in the beginning of fall quarter and in the community (your college or at I house) during. it is really fun and nice.
https://iseo.ucsd.edu/programs/ievents-calendar/index.html

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports, clubs (go to library walk and look for things)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do a lot of trips (go to Mexico!!, or any of the national parks)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy, I loved California, amazing place

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, talk to people, it is really easy and fun in the international community

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The mobility around. UCSD is gorgeous and La Jolla is really so so nice but getting further around takes time or requires a car. Living off campus could require a bike.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The chill life of Cali. It's beautiful and the vibe is super chill.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make a list of everything that has to be done and when. Everything will be fine in the end but try to be prepared to reduce stress. Consider staying for the grace period (the time you can stay before and after your stay on your visa)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for grants through legatbogen. Apply for many - you can reuse almost everything but it does take some time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world and therefore getting a connection to so many places around the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had a great time, would do it again any day:-)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
